page: OVHcloud r2-30 is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Haswell-generation processor running at a baseline clock rate of 2.2 GHz. The compute allocation consists of two dedicated physical cores mapped to two vCPUs with single-threaded execution at one thread per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while newer instructions like AVX-512 are not present.

The server delivers a prominent memory allocation of 30.0 GB of RAM, amounting to 15.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 50 GB SSD volume. The instance includes no GPU acceleration hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is reported at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

Empirical benchmark results demonstrate that computational throughput is limited by the dual-core topology and legacy CPU architecture. Synthetic compute scores placed the system in the lower percentiles, with multi-core Geekbench scoring 1760.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 1680.04. Memory bandwidth metrics indicate high throughput for cached 16 KB read blocks at 175.97 GB/sec, dropping to 7.81 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 10.54 GB/sec for writes. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server achieved 2.93 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.49 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure perspective, r2-30 delivers cost-efficient RAM capacity for applications requiring large working sets with modest compute demands. The system is suited for in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, caching layers, small database read replicas, and light ETL pipelines where memory density takes priority over processing speed.
description: OVHcloud r2-30 is a memory-optimized cloud server offering a dedicated dual-core Intel Haswell processor clocked at 2.2 GHz alongside 30 GB of RAM and 50 GB of local SSD storage. Hosted on the KVM hypervisor, each of the two vCPUs corresponds to a dedicated physical core without hyperthreading. The server emphasizes memory density, delivering 15 GB of RAM per core, but shows constrained computational throughput due to its dual-core topology and older processor microarchitecture. Benchmark evaluations place multi-core CPU metrics, including Geekbench (1760.0) and stress-ng (1680.04), within the bottom decile of tested systems, while uncached memory bandwidth reaches 7.81 GB/sec read and 10.54 GB/sec write. With no GPU acceleration and bundled local storage, r2-30 is designed for memory-intensive but compute-light applications such as dedicated Redis caching, memory-mapped data ingestion, and small transactional databases.
